dk-indopak-text.title: IndoPak (South Asian) Quran text
dk-indopak-text.note: Typeset after the IndoPak 'Quraan Al Majeed' mushaf. Displayed unmodified; we only split it into ayahs and words. This mushaf leaves Al-Fatihah's Bismillah unnumbered (and marks an alternate ayah end inside 1:7), so we number its ayahs 1:1–1:7 to match the Hafs (Kufan) count. Word boundaries re-aligned to Quran.com's word list in 4 ayahs (2:181, 8:6, 13:37, 72:16), where Quran.com joins two written words into one.

seerah-timeline.title: Seerah timeline (events and dated moments)
seerah-timeline.note: 23-year frame from Bukhari 3902. Dated moments only where a hadith states the time: Start of revelation, at the age of forty (Bukhari 3902). Khadija died three years before the migration (Bukhari 3896): 13 − 3 = year 10. He stayed in Makkah thirteen years, then was ordered to migrate (Bukhari 3902). Left for Makkah eight and a half years after the migration (Bukhari 4276): 13 + 8.5 = year 21.5. Lived as an emigrant ten years and died at sixty-three (Bukhari 3902): 13 + 10 = year 23. Events follow the order of Imam al-Bukhari's chapters (Book 1 'Revelation', Book 63 'Merits of the Ansar', Book 64 'Al-Maghazi'). That arrangement is mostly but not strictly chronological. Only the moments marked with a year are dated, each by a hadith that states the time. Each event lists the hadith of its Bukhari chapter (hadith-number range shown).

qac-ontology.title: Prophets in the Quran (who, and which ayahs mention them)
qac-ontology.publisher: Quranic Arabic Corpus: Ontology of Quranic Concepts (University of Leeds; maintained by Quran.com), GNU GPL
qac-ontology.note: Includes every concept in the ontology's Prophet or Messenger categories (24). Name variants grouped only where the ontology states (name-of …): ahmad → muhammad, israel → yaqub, messiah → jesus. Mentions are the ontology's word-level tags of references to each person (usually the name). For 'Israel', 41 mentions written as 'Bani Isra'il' (the Children of Israel, i.e. the people) are left out of Yaqub's list.

qac-morphology.title: Word roots, lemmas and parts of speech
qac-morphology.publisher: Quranic Arabic Corpus v0.4 (University of Leeds, Kais Dukes), GNU GPL
qac-morphology.note: Each word's root, lemma and part of speech, taken from the Corpus annotation and aligned 1:1 to our word list. 1642 roots, 49,967 word occurrences with a root. Arabic is converted from the Corpus's Buckwalter transliteration. Lemmas the Corpus tells apart only by a number (homographs such as EaAd/EaAd2) share one Arabic spelling and are shown together. Quranic Arabic Corpus (morphology, version 0.4), Copyright (C) 2011 Kais Dukes, GNU General Public License. Browse any root on corpus.quran.com to compare.

tadabbur-vocab.title: Most frequent words (word list and coverage)
tadabbur-vocab.publisher: Counted by Tadabbur from the Quranic Arabic Corpus (lemmas, roots) and Quran.com (word-by-word meanings)
tadabbur-vocab.note: Each dictionary form is counted over all 77,429 words of the Quran; 4,824 forms in total. Meanings are the word-by-word glosses Quran.com gives for that form's occurrences, most used first, shown as published. Coverage = occurrences / all words. Nothing here is written by us.
